This page documents a [[id:31C868B9-306E-4282-BA8C-07E647021B34][task]] in the [[id:A93B2CA2-66AB-4AD2-84EB-B41964980C57][Complete the ORE report configuration]] story. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance, and any notes or results.

* Goal

Codegen produces the FpML coded-scheme tables, their DQ artefact tables and
their notify triggers from models, so the "do not edit" comment on them is true
again.

* Acceptance

- Each of the fifteen refdata coded-scheme tables has an entity model, and its generated create, notify trigger, drop and DQ artefact files are identical to the current ones or differ only in ways recorded and explained.
- The hand-written =refdata_*_notify_trigger_create.sql= files for these tables are replaced by generated ones.
- The census reports none of these files as hand-written or as another generator's output.

* Result

Delivered by [[id:A31257E3-7495-46CD-B36D-10AA6D55CB09][Move the lookup artefact tables onto domain models]]
in sprint 28, not here. That task found the fifteen tables worse off than
this page recorded: they had no model at all, in any form, so nothing could
regenerate them and the JSON models this page blamed had never been in the
tree. It wrote all fifteen as =ores.codegen.entity= models under
=projects/ores.refdata/modeling/=, with the artefact hook and an =* Artefact
columns= section where the staging shape differs, and retired the legacy
=sql_schema_artefact_create= template with its literate source.

The acceptance holds as written: each of the fifteen has an entity model, its
generated create, notify trigger, drop and DQ artefact files match the
hand-written ones except the comment header and the model-stated staging
prose, and the census reports none of them as another generator's output.

This page's last open question was whether the tables belonged in refdata at
all. They do: the artefacts are FpML coded schemes, which is refdata's data,
and the fifteen publish into =ores.refdata= tables.

Closed on the strength of the task above. No work is owed here.
